sourceObjectiveEnglish: Prepare materials for a group: Usually add -s after a vowel and -es after a consonant.
sourceSpeakingEnglish: Role-play Cuatro compañeros with a patient classmate. Practice prepare materials for a group. Use this lesson's grammar, ask a related question, answer the partner, and confirm understanding. Keep language at beginner level; explain unfamiliar words in English when asked.

cards.proposalNote: Sac à dos is masculine; its plural is sacs à dos.
Le cours → les cours (no extra -s); la salle de classe → les salles de classe.
Il y a works for singular and plural.
La is a feminine article or object pronoun by context.
Use dans for inside (dans le sac à dos), sur for on top (sur la table), and à with a place (à l’école).
Sont can express identity, a condition, or a location; the surrounding words determine the meaning.
Sont can express condition or location; se trouvent emphasizes location. These are contextual alternatives, not separate verb classes.
Les is plural for any gender (les livres, les chaises); it can also mean them as an object pronoun.

candidateGrammar.explanation: French plural articles become les or des: le livre → les livres, une chaise → des chaises. Most nouns add written -s; nouns already ending in -s, -x or -z do not change (le cours → les cours). Nouns ending in -eau take -x (un tableau → des tableaux). In speech, plural is often heard in the article (le/la versus les) or liaison (les étudiants); the final -s is usually silent. Près des cahiers uses de + les, while des in des cahiers is an indefinite article. Il n’y a que means there are only, with no pas. Il nous faut means we need. Use il y a with singular or plural.

candidateGrammar.caution: In sac à dos, only sac changes: un sac à dos → des sacs à dos. Most written plural -s and -x endings are silent; the article often carries the audible number contrast. Les is the plural article for any gender.
